correctness.rationale: The exact polynomial follows from a disjoint trichotomy of independent sets. The nonvanishing proof checks all a,b>=0 and all Re(z)>=0 using s=|1+z| and the inequality 2|z|<=|1+z|^2, with strict gaps when a<b or a=b>2. Its remaining equality case a=b=2 is explicitly ruled out by z=±i substitution. A standalone exact coefficient census and independent rational Routh checks corroborate 81 and 256 finite profiles, respectively, but the proof itself covers all parameters. No unproved computational extension is used.

originality.rationale: The full strict left-half-plane theorem for all double-star parameters includes a genuinely new graph family with two adjacent branching vertices and arbitrarily large independent-set number. The recent exact-family spider theorem does not include those trees. The general published leaf-attachment enumerator already provides the polynomial identity (explicitly credited), but not its root-location conclusion. Bencs covers a symmetric special case. Actual published-finding corpus semantic queries and prior-claim searches found no equivalent or stronger coverage; alternate nomenclature/indexing remains a stated originality risk.

value.rationale: The Brown–Cameron characterization problem and the new spider theorem provide a specific graph-theoretic motivation for strict stability on diameter-three trees. The double stars with a,b>=2 have two branching centers and arbitrarily large independence number, so they form a genuinely different infinite structural family. Strict zero-freeness for all such trees is more than knowing their polynomial coefficients; it resolves a natural next case with an explicit complex-inequality proof, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
